content.about: The Comoros is a group of volcanic islands in the Indian Ocean, between Mozambique and Madagascar. Its islands have beaches, forests and an active volcano, Mount Karthala. It is a major producer of ylang-ylang, used in perfume. Arabic, French and Comorian are spoken.

standout.text: The coelacanth, a fish thought extinct for 66 million years, was rediscovered near the Comoros.

didYouKnow: Mount Karthala has one of the largest active volcanic craters.
Comoros is a major source of ylang-ylang oil.
Its name comes from the Arabic for "moon".
